extracted.intended_audience: prospective applicants to the EMBO Long-Term Fellowship (postdoctoral researchers in the molecular life sciences)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility rules for applying to the EMBO Long-Term Fellowship program, including nationality/host country constraints, mobility rules, application content/format restrictions, and administrative policies. Targeted at researchers planning to apply for an EMBO LTF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific scope
rubrics_metrics.description: EMBO funds basic research in the (molecular) life sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information on the EMBO subject areas is available on their website; contact fellowships@embo.org if in doubt whether your proposal falls within scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no age restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: EMBC Member States
rubrics_metrics.description: List of countries considered EMBC Member States (Austria, Belgium, Croatia, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Slovak Republic, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Turkey, United Kingdom).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These Member States are used for eligibility and host-country rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: EMBC Associate Member States
rubrics_metrics.description: India and Singapore are EMBC Associate Member States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associate member status affects eligibility in some cases (see nationality/host rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical degree (M.D.) eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants with a medical degree (M.D.) are eligible provided they have appropriate research experience comparable to a PhD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the fellowship office (fellowships@embo.org) prior to submission to confirm eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: PhD award country versus place of research — eligibility example (PhD officially from Spain but worked in Germany)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you received your PhD degree officially from Spain but spent the entirety of your PhD working in Germany, you may apply to go to a lab in Spain provided you can clearly show you spent the full duration working in Germany.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation showing where you carried out your PhD work may be required to determine eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobility requirement — cannot apply to continue working in same country as PhD/work
rubrics_metrics.description: If the country where you obtained your PhD is considered the country you normally work in, you cannot apply to continue working in that same country (mobility requirement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: receiving PhD officially from Spain but having worked entirely in Germany -> applying to Germany is not allowed because Germany is considered your country of work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicants with PhD performed in multiple countries
rubrics_metrics.description: If you performed your PhD in more than one country (e.g., worked in both France and Belgium), eligibility to apply for an EMBO LTF in a particular country is not auto-determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please contact the office (fellowships@embo.org) to determine your eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nationality: Non-EMBC nationals applying
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-EMBC nationals can apply only if they apply to go to a host lab in one of the EMBC Member States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nationality alone does not forbid application, but host-country must be an EMBC Member State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nationality: EMBC Associate Member nationals applying
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants whose nationality is from an EMBC Associate Member State (India, Singapore) may apply only if they apply to go to a host lab in one of the EMBC Member States or Associate Member State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-EMBC national with PhD from EMBC Member State cannot apply for fellowship in a Non-Member State
rubrics_metrics.description: A Non-EMBC national who had their PhD from an EMBC Member State is not eligible for a fellowship in a Non-Member State.

rubrics_metrics.name: EMBC Member State national who did PhD in Non-EMBC state cannot apply to work in another Non-Member State
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants need to be EMBC Member State nationals and need to have performed their PhD within one of the EMBC Member States in order to be eligible to apply for the fellowship to work in a Non-Member State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both nationality and PhD location conditions must be met to apply for a fellowship in a Non-Member State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior working time in host country — short-term exception
rubrics_metrics.description: You may move to a laboratory within the same country or apply to work in a country where you are already present only if you have not been working in the host country for more than 3 months prior to joining the host laboratory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule covers cases where you are already in the country but not established; if you've been working there more than 3 months, you are ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Returning to host country after long stays abroad — example denial
rubrics_metrics.description: If you worked in the host country for 14 months after your PhD, then for 2 months in another country, you cannot apply for the fellowship to go back to the host country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short interruptions elsewhere do not reset the mobility clock; eligibility is strict on prior duration in host country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reapplication limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Reapplication is allowed once irrespective of a change of project or host laboratory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can apply two times in total, provided that all eligibility criteria are met each time. A submission is counted as an application once receipt has been acknowledged and a reference number (ALTF number) has been assigned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent applications to other fellowships
rubrics_metrics.description: You may apply for other fellowships at the same time as applying for the EMBO Long-Term Fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As soon as you accept another fellowship you need to inform the EMBO Fellowship Office (fellowships@embo.org). Mention any other fellowship you are applying or planning to apply for in the online application form; this information is for statistical purposes and has no influence on evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior collaboration / co-publication with host supervisor
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have collaborated with the host supervisor before and have co-published, eligibility is not automatically determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please contact the office (fellowships@embo.org) to determine your eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration between several labs permitted but one official host/supervisor only
rubrics_metrics.description: You may apply with a research proposal that requires collaboration with other laboratories, but you can only have one official host lab and one official host supervisor in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the planned collaborations within the research proposal and choose one main supervisor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application formatting — no figures/tables/special formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not possible to add figures or tables or any special formatting in the application system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare your text to fit the plain application fields; do not expect to include embedded figures/tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-screening feedback policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications rejected at the pre-screening stage do not receive individual feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the prescreening stage there are no comments from the committee to provide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of journal impact factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Journal impact factors are not used in the evaluation and selection of applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EMBO encourages evaluation of the quality of the scientific work and its impact on the field, rather than the journal in which it was published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chances / success rate information
rubrics_metrics.description: EMBO receives on average 800 applications per deadline; the success rate was around 15% in the last selection round.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is statistical context, not an evaluative criterion; applicants should be aware of competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxation of fellowship stipend
rubrics_metrics.description: The EMBO fellowship is a research stipend and in principle should be tax exempt in most countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EMBO cannot advise on national tax regulations and recommends fellows contact the relevant authorities in the host country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial support exclusions (bench fees/overheads/consumables)
rubrics_metrics.description: The EMBO Long-Term Fellowship does not provide bench fees, overheads, funds for consumables, or any other financial benefits to the host supervisor/the receiving institute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel allowances
rubrics_metrics.description: EMBO does not offer any travel grants for fellowship holders to attend meetings, conferences or workshops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows should plan to seek other sources for travel funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contacting current fellows / data protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Due to data protection issues EMBO cannot give out contact details of EMBO fellows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful applicants are listed in the annual EMBO Facts & Figures available on the website for general information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public listing of successful applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful applicants are listed in the annual EMBO Facts & Figures report available on the EMBO website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the public source for names of successful fellows rather than direct contact information.
